comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff said BMS's own wording ('similar charges ... will likely occur in future periods') showed upfront and milestone R&D charges are recurring, and asked BMS to justify excluding them from non-GAAP.
comment_letters.company_answer: BMS first defended the exclusion, then agreed that from Q1 2022 non-GAAP would no longer adjust for upfront or contingent milestone payments on asset acquisitions or licenses.
comment_letters.next_filing_disclosure: Not checked in 10-K (non-GAAP sits in earnings releases); the Jan 2022 reply gives the excluded amounts.
comment_letters.why_it_matters: Same SEC sweep as PFE and LLY: big pharma's adjusted EPS excluded the cost of buying pipeline until 2022, flattering EPS-based pay and guidance.
comment_letters.impact_estimate: Licensing and asset acquisition R&D charges $1.1B (2020), $25M (2019), $1.0B (2018) = 9%, 0%, 18% of GAAP R&D (reply); quarterly up to 44% of R&D.
comment_letters.staff_quote: In this regard, your statement that "similar charges or gains were recognized in prior periods and will likely occur in future periods" appears to indicate that these R&D charges are inherently recurring in nature.
comment_letters.reply_quote: In response to the Staff's comment and as discussed with the Staff, beginning with BMS' earnings release for the quarter ended March 31, 2022, BMS will not include adjustments for R&D charges or other income resulting from upfront or contingent milestone payments in connection with asset acquisitions or licensing of third-party intellectual property rights in presentations of its non-GAAP measures.

comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff asked BMS to describe its Delaware exclusive-forum bylaw and whether it covers federal securities claims.
comment_letters.company_answer: BMS agreed to add the disclosures.
comment_letters.staff_quote: In future filings, please prominently describe the provision, including the relevant forum for litigation and any subject matter jurisdiction carve out, and whether this provision applies to actions arising under the Securities Act or Exchange Act.
comment_letters.reply_quote: The Company acknowledges the Staff's comment and will include these disclosures in future filings.

comment_letters.filing_reviewed: PREC14A filed by Starboard Value (activist), not by BMS
comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff told Starboard's counsel to support claims in its anti-Celgene-deal proxy, including its claim that BMS's base case was a 90% Revlimid revenue decline in 2026.
comment_letters.company_answer: No BMS reply: the letter is addressed to Starboard's counsel (Olshan Frome Wolosky), so it is not a BMS disclosure exchange.
comment_letters.why_it_matters: Context only: an outside claim that BMS modeled a 90% Revlimid revenue drop in 2026; Starboard, not BMS, made it.
comment_letters.staff_quote: On page 6, you state that based on your discussions with BSM management, you believe that their "base-case scenario" for the anticipated decline in REVLIMID revenues in 2026 is 90%."

comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff said it would not review the debt exchange S-4.
comment_letters.company_answer: Acceleration request and Exxon Capital representations (two CORRESP).
comment_letters.staff_quote: This is to advise you that we have not reviewed and will not review your registration statement.
